hook.text: Heat sugar past 170°C and it transforms—from white crystals to golden liquid to bitter black carbon.

buildup.text: Caramelization is the thermal decomposition of sugars. Hundreds of new flavor compounds are created.

discovery.text: Different sugars caramelize at different temperatures. Fructose starts at 110°C, sucrose at 160°C, glucose at 150°C.

twist.text: Caramelization is not the Maillard reaction. Caramel only involves sugar. Maillard needs sugar plus protein.

climax.text: The flavor of crème brûlée's burnt top, toffee, and caramel sauce all come from controlled sugar decomposition.

punchline.text: Sugar breaks down, flavor builds up. That's caramelization.

quiz.question: How does caramelization differ from the Maillard reaction?
options: Caramelization involves only sugar; Maillard needs sugar plus protein
